statement_en: Let $E_1,\cdots,E_n,\cdots \in \mathcal{F}$ be a decreasing sequence of sets, that is, $\cdots \subseteq E_n \subseteq \cdots \subseteq E_2\subseteq E_1$. Then the intersection is measurable. Moreover, if at least one set in the sequence has finite measure, then $$\mu\left(\bigcap_{n\geq 1}E_n\right)=\lim_{n\to \infty}\mu(E_n)=\inf_{n\geq 1}\mu(E_n).$$
